stem: Imran records craft-club stock as Beads $10$, Buttons $6$, and Ribbons $4$. The figure shows the bar graph he wants to match that table.

parts.text: Which claim correctly constructs a valid bar graph from that category-value table?

options.text: Put categories on one axis and counts on the other, use one uniform scale, and draw equal-width bars of heights $10$, $6$, and $4$.
The vertical axis label is the bar graph itself.
Draw bars of any widths, as long as the Beads bar is the tallest.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: A valid bar graph needs categories on one axis, counts on the other, one uniform scale, and equal-width bars whose heights match 10, 6, and 4.

teacher.key_rationale: Construction needs categories vs counts, a uniform scale, and equal-width bars matching 10, 6, and 4. Calling the axis label the graph swaps terms. Allowing any bar widths omits the equal-width condition.
teacher.figure_note: Added a three-category craft-club bar graph (Beads 10, Buttons 6, Ribbons 4) with equal bar widths and a uniform vertical scale.
